title: Fix snapshot script detection when sourcing files
description:
When `source("scripts/financials.R")` and `source("scripts/transparency.R")` run while another editor tab is active, snapshots can be redirected into that tab's directory. If source references are disabled, the call-stack fallback can also select an outer wrapper or fall back to `interactive`, creating new baselines instead of checking the intended ones.

Detect the active Quarto/knitr document first, then inspect the innermost `source()` or `sys.source()` frame for its input filename. Fall back to call-stack source references, then the active editor, then `interactive`. Explicit `script_name=` continues to override detection. Keep this fix separate from the trailing whitespace change in #56.

Regression coverage checks separate baselines for two scripts with the same snapshot name, both source-reference settings, nested sourcing, `sys.source()`, conflicting editor paths, document precedence, and explicit overrides. Update the generated documentation and changelog.

Validation on R 4.6.1:
- Full test suite passes with the documented sandbox cleanup warning, using `TMPDIR=/var/tmp` to avoid the stray `/tmp/.git` project marker.
- Air formatting and whitespace checks pass.
- CRAN-style package check: 0 errors, 1 warning, 0 notes. The warning is CRAN incoming feasibility: package version 0.3.2 already exists on CRAN.
- Direct reproduction with `keep.source = FALSE`: unchanged main detects `interactive`; this branch detects `actual.R`.

Existing snapshots under an incorrectly detected directory are not moved automatically; review them before relocating them to the intended script directory.

title: Fix false snapshot mismatches from trailing whitespace
description:
Printed model summaries and tibbles can add padding at the ends of lines, causing `snapshot()` to report differences when the output only gained or lost trailing spaces or tabs.

Normalize trailing spaces and tabs on both stored and newly generated snapshot lines. Existing baselines work without regeneration, while changes to values, indentation, internal spacing, and whitespace inside quoted strings still produce mismatches. Update the internal documentation and changelog.

Validation:
- All 116 snapshot assertions pass, including regression coverage for trailing spaces/tabs in either input and meaningful differences.
- Air formatting and whitespace checks pass.
- The full suite reports nine sandbox test failures and 17 warnings. The same failures and warnings reproduce on unchanged main in a separate checkout; they concern sandbox file lookup and are outside this change.

title: Fix unsafe snapshot defaults and start 0.3.1.9000
description:
Default snapshots could fail when a configured broom method required data, saved fit components, or did not support the model class. For example, a bare fixest snapshot called augment() without its required data.

- Keep tidy + glance and omit automatic augment for fixest, kmeans, drc, factanal, htest, speedlm, speedglm, and glmRob. Explicit augmentation remains available where supported.

description:

title: Fix session-dependent quotation marks in snapshots
description:
## Summary

Model-summary snapshots could differ between interactive R and Quarto solely because their `useFancyQuotes` settings differed. Set this option to `FALSE` during serialization and restore the caller's setting afterwards, including on failure. Document the behaviour in README and NEWS.

## Verification

- Regression tests compare model-summary snapshots with fancy quotes enabled and disabled and verify option restoration after success and failure.
- Package tests: 163 assertions passed; one documented sandbox-cleanup warning.
- Live Positron: the existing REF citation-comparison-models snapshot matches with `useFancyQuotes = TRUE` and warnings treated as errors; the setting remains TRUE afterwards. No baseline changes.
- CRAN-style check: zero errors, zero warnings, one development-version note. Air formatting and diff checks passed.

title: Make snapshot print limits configurable and session independent
description:
## Summary

Snapshot output previously inherited the R session's `max.print`, so identical data could produce a truncated baseline in one session and a mismatch during Quarto rendering in another. Set the printing limit locally using `snapshot.max_print` in the project configuration, defaulting to 1,000 entries, and restore caller options afterwards.

Validate configured limits and document entry counts, truncation, custom-method behaviour and baseline migration in the README, package help, vignette and NEWS. Leave the package's own configuration unchanged.

## Verification

- Full test suite: 158 passes, no failures, one expected sandbox-cleanup warning.
- CRAN-style check: no errors or warnings; one development-version NOTE.
- Regression coverage includes session independence, configured completeness, omitted-value changes, invalid limits, option restoration and explicit custom-method limits.
- REF report rendered successfully under session print limits of 1,000 and 10,000, using an explicit project limit of 2,000.

title: CRAN: release 0.3.0
Make snapshots Quarto-aware and stop renders on mismatches
description:
## Summary

- Detect the active Quarto document using `QUARTO_DOCUMENT_FILE`.
- Fall back to `knitr::current_input()` for direct knitr and R Markdown execution.
- Organize rendered snapshots under the source document filename instead of `interactive`.
- Add a distinct Quarto mode:
  - create missing snapshots automatically;
  - stop rendering with the full diff when an existing snapshot does not match.
- Support both knitr and Jupyter Quarto engines.
- Update tests, documentation, and `NEWS.md`.

## Verification

- `testthat::test_local(filter = "snapshot")`: 76 passed, 0 failed.
- Verified with a real Quarto render:
  - a missing snapshot was created successfully;
  - an edited snapshot stopped rendering with a nonzero exit status;
  - the mismatch remained visible with `warning: false` and `message: false`.
- `git diff --check` passed.

title: Add default methods
description:
This pull request introduces built-in class-based snapshot method defaults for serializing R objects, especially statistical models, using the `broom` package's functions. It updates the snapshotting infrastructure to use these sensible defaults when no explicit method is provided, and improves documentation to clarify the new behavior and detection of script names.

**Snapshot method defaults and serialization improvements:**

* Added a comprehensive set of class-based snapshot method defaults in `inst/extdata/snapshot-method-defaults.R`, using `broom::tidy`, `broom::glance`, and `broom::augment` for many common statistical model classes. This ensures informative and standardized output for a wide range of models.
* Updated `serialize_value()` to use these class defaults automatically when no `methods` argument is supplied, falling back to global defaults only if no class-specific default exists.
* Improved documentation for `serialize_value()` and `snapshot()` to describe the new class-based default behavior and the use of `broom` functions. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-75d495e8012b5bdfe09f60a1956144fac3e5fc3cfac6141678facc0b24800c07L7-R7) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-7ff0443177e0b3c89062108e77c9d58abb2b34530bce67de9f0e0ed4c315175bR49-R54) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-5d849f3782ddfdd6b0053b841b4be729f4fdaa33c9262caf6757aa185e5f5658R906-R911)

**Script name detection and documentation:**

* Clarified and documented the script name detection process in `snapshot()` and `get_snapshot_path()`, specifying the order of detection: RStudio active editor, call stack, then `"interactive"`. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-7ff0443177e0b3c89062108e77c9d58abb2b34530bce67de9f0e0ed4c315175bL15-R16) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-a9e3a80cb562877976a79e6e83f26fd8c786a165c1d20b2d995529f0e435eae3L13-R15) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-f44babab82d039179a51f45466acfa8b844aef8dfb6308854bfd30c62211d911R1-R18)

**Testing:**

* Updated tests to verify that global method defaults are used only when no class default exists, improving test coverage for the new behavior.

title: Refactor snapshot method selection to function-based API with generalized callable methods
description:
This change refactors `snapshot()` method selection from string-based method names to a generalized function-based API. Users now pass a function (or list of functions) directly, enabling any callable R method (for example, `length`, `print`, `summary`, custom functions) without maintaining a fixed method registry.

- **Function-based method API (breaking change)**
  - `method` now accepts:
    - a single function (e.g., `method = print`)
    - a non-empty list of functions (e.g., `method = list(print = print, summary = summary)`)
  - Character forms are no longer supported (including `"print"`, `"str"`, `"summary"`, expressions like `"print + str"`, and `"both"`).

- **Generalized dispatch + section headers**
  - Serialization now executes the provided callable(s) directly in order.
  - Section headers now use method names directly (e.g., `## print`, `## summary`, `## length`) instead of fixed labels like `## Object` / `## Structure`.
  - Method execution errors remain surfaced as class-aware snapshot errors.

- **Default behavior**
  - If `method` is omitted, snapshot uses default callable methods:
    - `list(print = base::print, str = utils::str)`

- **Configuration updates**
  - Snapshot config keys related to string-based method resolution are no longer used:
    - `snapshot.method`
    - `snapshot.method_by_class`
    - `snapshot.method_defaults_file`
  - `snapshot.dir` and other non-method config behavior remain unchanged.

- **Docs and tests**
  - Updated `snapshot()` and `serialize_value()` docs (roxygen + Rd), README, and vignette for the new function-based API.
  - Updated tests to:
    - validate function/list method inputs
    - validate generalized headers based on method names
    - remove deprecated string/alias behavior expectations
    - add coverage for method label inference and fallback naming for unnamed functions

```r
# Single callable
snapshot(model, "model_print", method = print)

# Multiple callables
snapshot(
  model,
  "model_multi",
  method = list(summary = summary, print = print, length = length)
)
```

title: default to both print and str
Fix CRAN submission issues: \dontrun → \donttest, interactive guard, user filespace transparency
description:
CRAN rejected the submission over three unaddressed policy issues: use of `\dontrun{}`, missing `if(interactive())` guards, and writing to user filespace without disclosure.

## Changes

- **`\dontrun{}` → `\donttest{}`** across all five exported functions (`find_root`, `snapshot`, `setup_sandbox`, `run_in_sandbox`, `cleanup_sandbox`) in both `.R` source and `.Rd` man files

- **User filespace — transparency over avoidance** — `snapshot()` must write to the project root by design (snapshots are persistent, version-controlled artifacts located via `find_root()`). Rather than hiding writes behind `tempdir()`, the docs now explicitly state this:
  > *"This function writes files to the user's project directory by design: snapshot files are meant to be persistent and committed to version control."*
  Same language added to `get_snapshot_path()` internals doc.

- **`if(interactive())`** — already correctly guarding `readline()` in the function body; documented explicitly in `cran-comments.md` to close the reviewer question

- **`cran-comments.md`** — updated with point-by-point responses to all three CRAN reviewer concerns

title: Rewrite package examples to be CRAN-executable via temp project helper
description:
CRAN feedback requested removing `\dontrun{}` usage for executable examples and avoiding writes to user home/package/getwd paths in examples/vignettes/tests. This PR switches examples to a temporary project workflow and aligns docs/tests around it.

- **New temp example workflow (`with_example`)**
  - Added exported `with_example(code, mismatch = FALSE)` to create a self-contained project under `tempdir()`, set working directory there for evaluation, and clean up afterward.
  - Generated example project includes:
    - `_resultcheck.yml` root marker
    - `analysis.R` with `snapshot(model, "model")`
    - snapshot fixtures (`model.md`, `model_mismatch.md`)
    - `tests/testthat/test-analysis.R`

- **Snapshot write-path behavior**
  - `snapshot()` now emits an interactive warning with the exact snapshot file path before writing/updating snapshots.
  - Default snapshot path remains `tests/_resultcheck_snaps` under project root and is configurable via `_resultcheck.yml` (`snapshot.dir`).
  - No default writes in examples to user home/package/getwd; examples run inside `with_example()`.

- **Sandbox/test integration semantics**
  - `setup_sandbox()` now supports empty sandboxes via no-arg usage: `setup_sandbox()`.
  - `run_in_sandbox()` now returns invisible `TRUE` on success, enabling direct `testthat` assertions instead of placeholder expectations.

- **Documentation and examples modernization**
  - Replaced `\dontrun{}` examples across `snapshot`, `find_root`, `setup_sandbox`, `run_in_sandbox`, and `cleanup_sandbox` with executable `with_example(...)` usage.
  - Split `snapshot()` documentation examples into three focused blocks:
    1. `method = "both"`, `"print"`, `"str"`
    2. matching run in sandbox (`mismatch = FALSE`)
    3. mismatch demonstration (`mismatch = TRUE`) behind `if (interactive())`
  - Updated README/vignette/man pages to consistently use `setup_sandbox()` (no file argument) for empty sandbox examples.
  - Added `man/with_example.Rd` and exported `with_example` in `NAMESPACE`.
  - Added namespace import for `stats::lm` and qualified `mtcars` usage in examples/helper-generated code to keep `R CMD check` clean.

- **Tests and CRAN-facing notes**
  - Updated sandbox tests to assert `expect_true(run_in_sandbox(...))`.
  - Reworked example-project tests to validate helper-created files and mismatch behavior using empty sandbox setup.
  - Updated `NEWS.md` and `cran-comments.md` with explicit notes about tempdir-based examples, configurable snapshot path defaults, and interactive write warnings.

```r
resultcheck::with_example({
  sandbox <- setup_sandbox()
  on.exit(cleanup_sandbox(sandbox), add = TRUE)

  # pass path
  expect_true(run_in_sandbox("analysis.R", sandbox))

  # optional mismatch demo (interactive docs use this pattern)
  if (interactive()) {
    file.copy(
      "tests/_resultcheck_snaps/analysis/model_mismatch.md",
      "tests/_resultcheck_snaps/analysis/model.md",
      overwrite = TRUE
    )
    run_in_sandbox("analysis.R", sandbox) # snapshot mismatch path
  }
})
```

Validated with:
- `testthat::test_local(...)` targeted runs for snapshot/sandbox/example-project changes
- `R CMD build .`
- `R CMD check --no-manual resultcheck_0.1.3.9000.tar.gz` (Status: OK)

title: Adopt `_resultcheck.yml` and move default snapshots to `tests/_resultcheck_snaps` (with legacy fallback)

This updates resultcheck’s project conventions by standardizing on `_resultcheck.yml` and changing default snapshot storage from repository root to `tests/_resultcheck_snaps`. It also adds explicit configurability for snapshot location while preserving compatibility with existing `resultcheck.yml` users.

  - `snapshot.dir` config added under `_resultcheck.yml` to override snapshot location.
  - Path resolution supports both relative (to project root) and absolute directory values.

- **Documentation and release notes**

  - `NEWS.md` includes explicit `0.1.4` entries for:

- **Tests**

title: Add `method` parameter to `snapshot()` for print-only or str-only serialization
description:
Some objects (e.g. `tinytable`) embed volatile, session-specific values (random IDs, temp paths) in their `str()` output, making snapshots non-reproducible across runs. `snapshot()` had no way to opt out of either serialization method.

## Changes

- **`serialize_value(value, method)`** — new `method` argument (`"both"` | `"print"` | `"str"`); `"both"` preserves existing type-specific behavior
- **`snapshot(..., method = c("both", "print", "str"))`** — exposes `method` as a user-facing parameter; passes it through to `serialize_value()`
- **Docs** — roxygen and README updated; README includes a method reference table
- **Tests** — 3 new tests covering header content for each method and end-to-end file output

## Usage

```r
# Avoid volatile str() output (e.g. tinytable with session paths / random IDs)
snapshot(my_table, "my_table", method = "print")

# Capture only structural repr, skip print output
snapshot(my_model, "my_model_struct", method = "str")

# Default: existing behavior unchanged
snapshot(my_df, "my_df")
```

title: Fix snapshot instability for statistical models by serializing structured data
description:
Snapshots for `lm`/`glm` models were unstable across platforms due to formatted `summary()` output containing locale-dependent quotation marks in "Signif. codes" line and inconsistent numeric formatting.

## Changes

- **Modified `serialize_value()` in `R/snapshot.R`**
  - Extract structured components (coefficients, R-squared, sigma, df, fstatistic) from summary object
  - Serialize coefficients using controlled `sprintf()` formatting instead of `print()`
  - Use `%.10g` precision for all numeric values to ensure consistency
  - Exclude "Signif. codes" line entirely

- **Updated README**
  - Document that models use structured serialization for cross-platform stability

## Example

Before: Formatted summary with platform-dependent symbols
```r
Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
```

After: Structured data with controlled precision
```r
### Coefficients
                      Estimate     Std. Error        t value       Pr(>|t|)
(Intercept)        37.28512617    1.877627337    19.857575268.241798845e-19
wt                -5.344471573   0.5591010451   -9.5590441471.293958701e-10

### Model Statistics
R-squared: 0.7528327937
F-statistic: 91.375325 on 1 and 30 DF
```

Snapshots now match reliably across platforms while remaining human-readable.

title: Fix R CMD check failures: non-ASCII chars, missing imports, and test state pollution
description:
R CMD check was failing with warnings (non-ASCII characters, missing imports) and test failures caused by state pollution between tests where `getwd()` returned `NULL`.

## Changes

**Package compliance**
- Replaced Unicode symbols (✓, ✗, ⚠) with escape sequences (`\u2713`, `\u2717`, `\u26a0`) in `R/snapshot.R`
- Added `importFrom` directives for `utils::{getSrcref, str}` and `grDevices::{pdf, dev.off}`

**Test infrastructure**
- Removed `test-snapshot-old.R` and `test-integration-old.R` (used obsolete API with `interactive` parameter and `.rds` files)
- Refactored tests to call functions directly instead of sourcing scripts, avoiding environment context issues

**State management**
- Enhanced `find_root()` to validate stored working directory paths before use, falling back to `getwd()` if path no longer exists
- Improved cleanup in `run_in_sandbox()` to ensure `.resultcheck_env$.resultcheck_original_wd` is reset even on error
- Fixed `on.exit()` ordering in integration test to restore working directory before deleting temp directory

The issue manifested when `run_in_sandbox()` stored a reference to a temp directory in `.resultcheck_env$.resultcheck_original_wd`, then deleted the directory. Subsequent tests calling `find_root()` would use this stale path, causing `getwd()` to fail.

**Results**: R CMD check now passes with 0 errors, 0 warnings. All 54 tests pass.

title: Add interactive snapshotting for empirical analysis workflows
description:
Enables empirical researchers to track analysis outputs during interactive development and verify them in automated tests. Snapshots are stored as human-readable, git-friendly `.md` files.

## Implementation

**Core Functions**
- `find_root()` - Locates project root via `resultcheck.yml`, `.Rproj`, or `.git` using rprojroot
- `snapshot(value, name)` - Context-aware snapshotting that:
  - **Interactive mode**: Warns and prompts to update when differences found
  - **Testing mode** (inside `run_in_sandbox()`): Errors if snapshot missing or doesn't match

**Storage Structure**
```
_resultcheck_snapshots/          # gitignored by default
  script_name/
    snapshot_name.md             # Human-readable text format
```

Snapshots organized by script name; serializes objects to human-readable text using `str()`, `print()`, `summary()`.

## Usage

**Interactive Development**
```r
# In analysis.R
model <- lm(mpg ~ wt + hp, data = mtcars)
snapshot(model, "regression_model")
# First run: ✓ New snapshot saved
# Later runs: Warning with differences, prompts to update
```

**Automated Testing**
```r
test_that("analysis produces stable results", {
  sandbox <- setup_sandbox(c("data/input.rds"))
  
  # analysis.R contains snapshot() calls
  # Will ERROR if snapshots don't match
  run_in_sandbox("analysis.R", sandbox)
  
  cleanup_sandbox(sandbox)
})
```

## Workflow

1. Run analysis scripts interactively → creates `.md` snapshot files
2. Run same scripts in sandbox/testing → errors if snapshots don't match
3. When analysis changes, re-run interactively to review and update snapshots

## Changes

- **Dependencies**: Added rprojroot; waldo optional for better diffs
- **New**: `R/snapshot.R` with context-aware snapshot infrastructure
- **Modified**: `run_in_sandbox()` stores original working directory for `find_root()` to work in sandboxes
- **Tests**: New tests for snapshot functionality and sandbox integration
- **Docs**: Updated README with workflow examples, added `resultcheck.yml.example` template

title: Add path validation to prevent sandbox escape via absolute paths and traversal
description:
The `setup_sandbox()` function accepted absolute paths and path traversal sequences (`..`), allowing files to be copied outside the sandbox boundary, contradicting the documentation stating only relative paths are supported.

## Changes

**Path Validation**
- Reject absolute paths (Unix `/path`, Windows `C:\path` and `\\UNC`)
- Split paths by separators and reject components matching exactly `..` (allows filenames like `file..txt`)

**Implementation Details**
- Pre-copy validation only (checks paths before use)
- Component-based `..` detection prevents path traversal while allowing legitimate filenames
- `file.copy()` follows symlinks and copies content (not the link itself), ensuring files stay in sandbox

**Tests**
- Absolute path rejection (both platforms)
- Path traversal rejection (basic and nested: `../x`, `a/../../b`)
- Legitimate double-dot filenames (`file..txt`, `subdir/data..csv`)
- Symlink handling verification

```r
# Before: silently accepts dangerous paths
setup_sandbox("/etc/passwd")  # Could copy outside sandbox

# After: errors immediately
setup_sandbox("/etc/passwd")
# Error: Absolute paths are not allowed. Please use relative paths only: /etc/passwd

setup_sandbox("../sensitive/data")
# Error: Path traversal (e.g., '..') is not allowed for security reasons: ../sensitive/data
```

## Security

The validation prevents security issues by:
1. Rejecting absolute paths (prevents files from being copied outside sandbox)
2. Rejecting `..` in path components (prevents path traversal attacks)
3. Using `file.path(temp_dir, file)` to construct all target paths (ensures files go into sandbox)
4. Using `file.copy()` which follows symlinks and copies content (prevents symlink escape)

All paths are validated to be relative without `..` components before use, and the temp_dir is created by the function itself, ensuring files cannot escape the sandbox.

title: Add sandboxing functions for isolated empirical analysis testing
description:
Implements three functions to enable isolated testing of empirical analysis scripts: sandbox setup, script execution, and cleanup.

## Changes

- **`setup_sandbox(files, temp_base = NULL)`** - Creates temp directory, copies files preserving directory structure, returns sandbox object with path and unique ID
- **`run_in_sandbox(script_path, sandbox = NULL, ...)`** - Executes script in sandbox via `withr::with_dir()`, suppressing messages/warnings/graphics
- **`cleanup_sandbox(sandbox = NULL, force = TRUE)`** - Removes sandbox directory

All functions default to last-created sandbox when `sandbox` param omitted, stored in package environment.

## Dependencies

- `withr` (Imports)
- `testthat >= 3.0.0` (Suggests)

## Example

```r
library(resultcheck)
library(testthat)

test_that("fiscal script produces reproducible results", {
  sandbox <- setup_sandbox(c(
    "data/panel_data_pca.rds",
    "data/fiscal.dta",
    "save/regModels.RData"
  ))
  
  run_in_sandbox("code/fiscal.R", sandbox)
  
  expect_true(file.exists(file.path(sandbox$path, "data/panel_data_fiscal.rds")))
  
  original <- readRDS("data/panel_data_fiscal.rds")
  regenerated <- readRDS(file.path(sandbox$path, "data/panel_data_fiscal.rds"))
  expect_equal(dim(original), dim(regenerated))
  
  cleanup_sandbox(sandbox)
})
```

## Testing

15 test cases covering directory creation, file copying, script execution, error handling, and full workflow integration.
